answer: The first-line treatment for generalized anxiety disorder includes guided self-help and psychoeducation. If symptoms persist, high-intensity psychological therapy (CBT) or medication (an SSRI) is recommended, with CBT and medication considered equally effective first-line options for moderate to severe cases [NICE, 2019].

Intramuscular epinephrine in the anterolateral thigh is the first-line treatment for anaphylaxis and should not be delayed. Antihistamines and corticosteroids are adjunctive only and do not replace epinephrine as the immediate emergency treatment.
